/portfolio_intel/about.description:
Return the extension name, version, and scope.

Health-check command used by the M0 gate demo and by every derived
analytic to stamp its response envelope with the extension version
that produced it (per PRD §4 Guiding Principle 3 — deterministic
outputs).

Matches the ``@router.command(methods=["GET"])`` signature of
``openbb_backtest.backtest_router.about`` — passing ``model=<str>``
triggers OpenBB's standard-models registry lookup, which fails for
extension-local models (PR #466 review finding 4).

/regime/detect.description: Detect the current MarketRegime from SPY + VIX daily bars.
/regime/detect.examples:
Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# Current market regime
obb.regime.detect()
# Regime as of a historical date (backtesting)
obb.regime.detect(as_of=2020-03-16)
```

standard.name: as_of
standard.description: ISO-format date (``YYYY-MM-DD``) to snap the classification to. Defaults to today. Useful for backtesting or auditing a historical regime call.

standard.name: lookback_days
standard.description: Days of daily bars to fetch. Must be >= 233 (200d SMA + 33d walkback window). Default 400 gives a comfortable margin over weekends and holidays.

standard.name: spy_symbol
standard.description: Symbol for the broad market index. SPY is the standard.

standard.name: vix_symbol
standard.description: Symbol for the volatility index. The ``^VIX`` prefix works with yfinance / fmp_cached; users on other providers may need a different ticker convention.

standard.name: provider
standard.description: OpenBB data provider. Defaults to ``"fmp_cached"`` (matches CLAUDE.md's Provider rule — see :data:`_DEFAULT_PROVIDER`). Callers can override explicitly for R&D use cases, but downstream Analysis + techtrade consumers assume fmp_cached response shapes.

/techtrade/segments.description: list supported GICS segments and their (placeholder) resolved universes.

standard.name: universe_source
standard.description: How each segment universe is resolved (``etf_holdings`` / ``constituent_list`` / ``screener``). Defaults to ``"etf_holdings"``.

standard.name: rank_metric
standard.description: Metric used to rank movers within a segment (``pct_change`` / ``volume`` / ``gap`` / ``rel_volume``). Defaults to ``"pct_change"``.

standard.name: top_n
standard.description: Number of top movers to keep per segment. Defaults to ``10``.

/techtrade/movers.description:
Rank the day's top movers for one or all GICS segments (PRD §10, issue #70).

Ranks a single GICS sector when ``segment`` is given, or all 11 sectors in
canonical order when ``segment`` is ``None``. The requested ``as_of`` is snapped
back to the most recent trading session before ranking, so the result is always
look-ahead-free.

standard.name: segment
standard.description: A single GICS sector name (e.g. ``"Information Technology"``) to rank, or ``None`` to rank all 11 sectors. Defaults to ``None``.

standard.name: metric
standard.description: Metric used to rank movers within each segment (``pct_change`` / ``volume`` / ``gap`` / ``rel_volume``). Defaults to ``"pct_change"``.

standard.name: top_n
standard.description: Number of top movers to keep per segment. Defaults to ``10``.

standard.name: as_of
standard.description: ISO date to rank as of; snapped to the most recent session. Defaults to today when ``None``.

/techtrade/signals.description:
Compute ranked confluence signals for a symbol set or a GICS segment (PRD §12.3, issue #75).

Scores either an explicit ``symbols`` set or a ``segment``'s ranked top movers with the
#74 confluence engine under the named ``preset``, then ranks the results by signed score
descending (most-long first) into a contiguous ``rank_in_segment``. Each returned signal
carries the per-indicator votes -- with the preset's weight tilt visible in every
``vote.weight`` -- so the engine can always answer *"why long?"*. The requested ``as_of``
is snapped back to the most recent trading session before scoring, so the result is
always look-ahead-free.

standard.name: segment
standard.description: A single GICS sector name (e.g. ``"Information Technology"``) to resolve into its ranked top movers, or ``None`` to score an explicit ``symbols`` set. Defaults to ``None``.

standard.name: symbols
standard.description: Explicit instrument symbols to score; takes precedence over ``segment``. Defaults to ``None``.

standard.name: preset
standard.description: Named confluence preset: ``"trend_follow"`` (default, the Q4 base) / ``"mean_revert"`` / ``"breakout"``. Each re-tilts the same four indicator families toward a style.

standard.name: as_of
standard.description: ISO date to score as of; snapped to the most recent session. Defaults to today when ``None``.

/techtrade/plan.description:
Assemble per-symbol trade plans for a symbol set or a GICS segment (PRD §9.2, issue #77).

Runs the #75 confluence signal chain under the named ``preset`` over either an explicit
``symbols`` set or a ``segment``'s ranked top movers, then assembles one ``TradePlan`` per
ranked signal -- sizing the #76 stop / target / quantity at ``risk`` of notional, mapping the
broker-ready order legs, and attaching an inline recommendation. The plans preserve the signal
chain's ranking order. The requested ``as_of`` is snapped back to the most recent trading
session before scoring, so each plan is look-ahead-free.

standard.name: segment
standard.description: A single GICS sector name (e.g. ``"Information Technology"``) to resolve into its ranked top movers, or ``None`` to plan an explicit ``symbols`` set. Defaults to ``None``.

standard.name: symbols
standard.description: Explicit instrument symbols to plan; takes precedence over ``segment``. Defaults to ``None``.

standard.name: preset
standard.description: Named confluence preset: ``"trend_follow"`` (default) / ``"mean_revert"`` / ``"breakout"``.

standard.name: risk
standard.description: Fraction of notional risked per trade, fed to the #76 sizing. Defaults to ``0.01``.

standard.name: as_of
standard.description: ISO date to plan as of; snapped to the most recent session. Defaults to today when ``None``.

/techtrade/orders.description:
Materialize the broker-ready order legs of a single trade plan (PRD §9.2, issue #77).

Re-validates the supplied ``plan`` (an in-memory :class:`TradePlan` or one deserialized from
JSON) and returns its order legs unchanged -- an idempotent round-trip. A flat plan carries no
position and yields an empty list.

standard.name: plan
standard.description: The trade plan whose orders to materialize.

/techtrade/simulate.description:
Paper-fill a set of order legs against a forward OHLCV window (PRD §14.1, issue #78).

Drives the #78 :class:`~openbb_techtrade.execution.broker.PaperBroker` over ``bars`` (whose
first row is the next-bar-open session *t+1*): fills the ``entry`` leg at ``bars[0]`` open with
adverse slippage, then walks the contingent ``exit_stop`` / ``exit_target`` / ``exit_time`` legs
bar-by-bar, taking the first triggered exit with a conservative stop-wins tie-break. The signal
bar *t* is never read, so the result is no-look-ahead by construction. An empty order list (a
flat plan) yields an empty Filllist.

standard.name: orders
standard.description: The canonical #77 order legs to simulate (entry first, then contingent exits).

standard.name: bars
standard.description: The forward OHLCV window starting at *t+1*; each bar carries ``open`` / ``high`` / ``low`` and a ``timestamp`` or ``date``.

/techtrade/scan.description:
Screen all 11 GICS sectors into a cross-segment ranked plan list (PRD §9.2, issue #79).

The one-call orchestrator: ranks each sector's top ``top_n`` movers by ``metric``, runs them
through the #75 signals -> #76 rules/sizing -> #77 orders chain, optionally paper-fills via #78,
then returns the actionable plans **cross-segment ranked** by ``|signal.score|`` descending
(symbol, then segment, tie-break). ``metric`` selects *which movers* per sector enter the chain;
it is **not** the cross-segment plan-rank key. ``as_of`` is snapped once to the last ``XNYS``
session (look-ahead-free) and threaded to every sector. ``simulate=False`` returns the order
skeletons only; ``limit`` slices the top of the ranked list. Skipped sectors / symbols (transient
fetch failures) surface in ``OBBject.warnings`` rather than aborting the scan.

standard.name: metric
standard.description: Mover rank metric (``pct_change`` / ``volume`` / ``gap`` / ``rel_volume``). Defaults to ``"pct_change"``.

standard.name: top_n
standard.description: Per-segment mover cap. Defaults to ``10`` (up to ``11 x top_n`` plans returned, sorted).

standard.name: preset
standard.description: Confluence/rule preset. Defaults to ``"trend_follow"``.

standard.name: risk
standard.description: Risk-per-trade fraction for #76 sizing; ``None`` uses the chain default ``0.01``.

standard.name: as_of
standard.description: ISO date to scan as of; snapped to the most recent session. Defaults to today when ``None``.

standard.name: simulate
standard.description: Request inline #78 fills. Defaults to ``True``. NOTE (v1): the live command does not yet fetch forward (``t+1...``) bars, so no fills are attached over the HTTP surface regardless of this flag -- the ranked order skeletons are returned either way. The live forward-bar fetcher is a tracked follow-up; the ``scan_segments`` ``bars=`` seam already fills when a window is supplied (exercised offline).

standard.name: limit
standard.description: Optional global top-of-list slice after the cross-segment sort. Defaults to ``None``.

/techtrade/export.description:
Write the 6-sheet recommendation workbook to disk (PRD §14.3, issue #81).

Renders ``plans`` as a polished, deterministic ``.xlsx`` workbook with six sheets
(``Recommendations`` / ``Levels`` / ``Reasoning`` / ``Orders`` / ``Fills`` / ``Summary``),
a compliance disclaimer on the Recommendations sheet (locked by PRD §20 Q9), conditional
formatting (color-coded Action, R:R data bar, score color scale, etc.), and a frozen + filterable
header row. Rows are sorted by ``segment`` → ``conviction`` → ``action`` → ``symbol`` so the
workbook is byte-stable for identical inputs (design L6).

Money / quantities stay :class:`~decimal.Decimal` end-to-end; cells store the unrounded
``float(Decimal)`` and Excel ``number_format`` controls display rounding only -- the model value
is always the source of truth (design Q-E / L9). The only datetime cell is the deterministic
:class:`~openbb_techtrade.models.Fill` ``timestamp`` (#78 Q-F session-close localization), never
a wall-clock; the filename date is the run's ``as_of`` (design L4).

standard.name: plans
standard.description: Paper-filled trade plans -- typically the output of :func:`obb.techtrade.scan` (#79) or :func:`obb.techtrade.plan` (#77). Each plan carries the ``recommendation``, ``signal.votes``, ``orders``, and ``simulated_fills`` that feed the six sheets. An empty list yields a header-only workbook (still containing the disclaimer).

standard.name: path
standard.description: Explicit output path. Overrides the ``ExportConfig`` default of ``Analysis/exports/techtrade_<as_of>.xlsx`` (design L4 / Q-F). The parent directory is auto-created. A same-as-of run overwrites silently (deterministic, re-runnable artifact).

standard.name: engine
standard.description: Workbook engine: ``"openpyxl"`` (default, core dependency, full conditional formatting, design L1 / Q-B B1) or ``"xlsxwriter"`` (optional, lazy-imported, best-effort richer formatting -- no parity guarantee).

/techtrade/validate.description:
Robustness-validate a TradePlan via openbb-backtest (PRD §15, issue #82).

Translates ``plan`` into a :class:`~openbb_backtest.models.BacktestConfig` (universe
``[plan.symbol]``, window ``[as_of - horizon_years, as_of]``, strategy
``techtrade_confluence``), calls ``openbb-backtest``'s ``validate`` over WFO / CPCV
folds, attaches the returned :class:`~openbb_backtest.models.ValidationReport` to
``plan.validation`` via :meth:`~pydantic.BaseModel.model_copy` (immutable
discipline), and returns the verdict.

The reported ``verdict`` is one of ``"robust"`` / ``"fragile"`` / ``"overfit"``,
derived by ``openbb-backtest``'s gate (precedence ``overfit > robust > fragile``);
the effective thresholds are recorded on ``report.thresholds`` so the verdict is
auditable. techtrade does not re-implement the gate (design L4 / L5).

standard.name: plan
standard.description: The plan to validate (single-symbol, single ``as_of``).

standard.name: method
standard.description: Resampling method: ``"wfo"`` (default) or ``"cpcv"``. Forwarded 1:1 to backtest's validator.

standard.name: thresholds
standard.description: Verdict-threshold overrides merged over backtest's defaults (``pbo_robust`` / ``pbo_overfit`` / ``dsr_robust`` / ``dsr_overfit``). ``None`` uses backtest's defaults (design L5).

standard.name: horizon_years
standard.description: Number of years of history to span the folds (default 5).

standard.name: provider
standard.description: Data provider for the fold history; ``None`` uses backtest's default (``fmp_cached`` in this fork).

/techtrade/tune.description:
Tune indicator periods for a GICS segment, gated by #82's validate (PRD §12.4, §15).

Steps (design §4.1):

1. Pool the segment's universe OHLCV into ``(X, y)`` (L4 + Q-C horizon
 window + Q-B forward-return target).
2. Fit tuneta over the L6 8-knob search space -> candidate IndicatorConfig.
3. Build a sample TradePlan for the segment's benchmark ETF (Q-A A1).
4. ``with tune_override({segment: candidate}):`` make the candidate
 visible to the validate fold loop without writing to disk first
 (§5.3 W2 -- safe because #82's fold loop is sequential in-thread).
5. ``validate_plan(plan, method=method, thresholds=thresholds,
 horizon_years=horizon_years, provider=provider)`` -> verdict.
6. Gate: if verdict == "robust" AND the candidate genuinely differs from
 DEFAULT_CONFIG (Q-F guard 3) -> persist via write_tuned. Otherwise
 persisted=False + a diagnostic reason string. Logged at WARNING on
 fragile/overfit so a long loop is visible without an exception.
7. Return OBBject[TuningReport].

Raises
------
TechtradeDependencyError
 When ``tuneta`` is not installed (raised by fit_segment via
 :func:`_require_tuneta`); or when ``openbb-backtest`` is not installed
 (raised by validate_plan via #82's ``_require_backtest``). The error
 message names the specific extra; for a full tune the user needs both
 ``[tuneta]`` and ``[validation]``.
ValueError
 If ``segment`` is not one of the 11 GICS sectors in
 :data:`SEGMENT_BENCHMARK_ETFS` (Q-A A1).
